messages.content: 創建一個藍色背景的正方形畫作，尺寸為16x16英吋，然後以70％的屏幕亮度顯示30秒。

function.name: painting_create
function.description: Creates a new painting with specified parameters Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

shape.description: Shape of the painting to be created.

dimensions.description: Dimensions of the painting in inches.

function.name: display_set_screen_brightness
function.description: Sets the screen brightness for viewing the painting Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

duration.description: Duration to maintain the brightness level in seconds.

function.name: painting_display
function.description: Displays a created painting for a specific amount of time Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

time.description: Time in seconds the painting will be displayed for.

message.reasoning:
The user wants to create a painting with shape square, background color blue, dimensions 16x16 inches. Then set screen brightness to 70% for duration? The user says "display 30 seconds". So we need to call painting_create, then display_set_screen_brightness, then painting_display.

We should use the functions accordingly. The painting_create expects shape, background_color, dimensions array. We'll pass shape="square", background_color="blue", dimensions=[16,16].

Then display_set_screen_brightness expects percentage and duration. We want 70% brightness for 30 seconds? Actually the user said "display 30 seconds" after setting brightness. But the function display_set_screen_brightness has duration parameter. We can set it to 30 seconds. Then painting_display expects time in seconds. We also want 30 seconds. But maybe we don't need to set brightness again? The user might want to set brightness to 70% for 30 seconds, then display painting for 30 seconds. So we can do:

1. painting_create
2. display_set_screen_brightness(percentage=70, duration=30)
3. painting_display(time=30)

Let's do that.
